content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have six [product_name] modules (version [version_no]) and one [product_name] HMI panel. I want to be able to switch between these six modules while the system is operating, using the HMI—essentially, I’d like to set up six buttons or pages on the panel to navigate between them. All controllers are running the same program. Is there a way to achieve this? Thank you.

This can be done, but you cannot start or stop the running [product_name] program directly from the HMI. You'd need to configure a virtual input in each [product_name] and use logic blocks to simulate inactivity, so it appears as though the module is not functioning when desired.
Hello, I do not need to start or stop the module, I just want to control six [product_name] units on six different pages. Could you explain further how to set this up? Thank you.

Yes, but this is more a matter of configuring the HMI than the [product_name] modules. On the HMI, you can create buttons (Button1 for Page1, Button2 for Page2, etc.) for each [product_name] module. Each page can have settings specific to one module. To program your HMI, you will need suitable engineering software (e.g., [product_name] programming tool).

With a Basic Panel, up to four communication connections can be established. With Comfort Panels, you can have up to eight. If you want each of the six [product_name] modules to communicate with the panel individually, you’ll need a Comfort Panel.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to manage six [product_name] modules individually via a single HMI by giving each one its own dedicated page or button. Forum members clarify that the HMI can be configured for this kind of navigation, but the actual number of supported connections will depend on the hardware. There is some ambiguity about what features are standard and which components or configuration are needed for full multi-module control.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates straightforward switching and management of six [product_name] modules from an HMI panel, with each module accessible through its own page or button.
